newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Soaring U.S. trade gap hits dlr, shares fall.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Soaring U.S. trade gap hits dlr, shares fall.

text.p: News that the U.S. trade deficit has surged to its highest level in more than eight years caused a wave of selling on Wednesday, sending the dollar below 110 yen and 1.51 marks. The Commerce Department said soaring imports, including costlier foreign oil, caused the shortfall on trade with the rest of the world in July to shoot up 42.6 percent to $11.68 billion -- far above the $8.8 billion forecast by Wall Street economists. The deficit was the highest since late 1987.
The July trade deficit with Japan also widened sharply, up 32.9 percent to $4.31 billion, helping to slash more than one yen in value off the U.S. currency.
A large trade deficit tends to depress the dollar's value because when a country imports more than it exports, dollars flow out into the currency market to pay for the imports.

Prior to the trade news, the currency markets had been moribund, with the dollar stuck in a tight range around levels seen late on Tuesday. Talk of a possible U.S. Federal Reserve rate rise was completely dominating transactions.

This followed comments on Tuesday by an unnamed Fed official to Reuters that eight of the 12 district banks in the Federal Reserve System have requested a rise in the 5.0 percent discount rate. The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meets on September 24 and while the market has changed its mind several times about the likelihood of a rate rise, it now believes one is definitely in the offing.
Analysts said that if the discount rate was raised it would suggest that the trend of U.S. rates had decisively turned, with serious implications for investors.

Meanwhile, the official release on Wednesday of the extensively-leaked French budget had little effect on the franc. It retreated just over a centime from six-week highs at 3.3957 per mark set on Tuesday.

On the European bourses, leading shares all closed lower after the renewed U.S. rate jitters put the brakes on Wall Street's recent surge. New York stocks opened mixed and then fell further. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was about 10 points down by the time London share trading ended.

In London, stronger-than-expected British retail sales pushed down government bonds and stocks early in the day, though analysts said the figures were not likely to have much impact on monetary policy.
"Trading is quiet, People don't think the retail sales numbers are going to change very much and it was really just an excuse to mark the market lower," said one senior trader.
The blue chip FTSE 100 index increased its losses as the session progressed to close down 16.6 points, or 0.42 percent.

In Frankfurt, German shares ended what was described as listless bourse trade slightly lower. The market eased further in post-bourse electronic trading, undermined by the weakening dollar which makes German exports less attractive.
Dealers said they did not expect major pressure on German shares, however, and current levels were expected to hold though the end of the week
On the Paris bourse, shares closed lower in line with losses posted on Wall Street. The publication of the French budget, which weighed on bonds, also affected stock prices.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 8.13 points or 0.39 percent at 2,072.73. One bright point was Alcatel Alsthom, which moved higher after announcing bid to buy Thomson SA and turn it into European defence leader.

On the energy market, traders said oil prices were likely to stay firm for the rest of the year even if the military confrontation between Iraq and the United States was defused, thanks to bullish supply-demand fundamentals.

Lingering concerns over tight heating oil stocks approaching the winter and an indefinite delay to the UN's Iraqi oil-for- food arrangement should keep world benchmark North Sea Brent blend over $20 a barrel for the next few weeks, they said.
CURRENCIES
The dollar was at 1.5091 marks and 109.12 yen compared with 1.5147 marks and 110.35 yen late in Europe on Tuesday .
STOCK MARKETS
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares closed 16.6 points down at 3,955.7.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index closed 8.13 points down at 2,072.73.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed down 2.38 at 2,625.70
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed in London at $383.35 against $383.55 at Tuesday's close. Silver ended two cents firmer at $5.09.
